title: Verify metering correctness under backpressure and windowing semantics
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Prove that the end-to-end metering pipeline produces correct input/output token accounting when the serving layer experiences sustained backpressure, windowed aggregation, or late-arriving fragments. Motivation: We observe sporadic charge mismatches for long-running streaming sessions under high load. Hypothesis: interactions between rate-limiter-induced delays, sliding window aggregation in the aggregator service, and out-of-order fragment delivery create edge cases where input tokens or prefix credits are double-counted or dropped during checkpoint compaction.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic test harness reproduces the original mismatch scenario with synthetic clients and controlled backpressure
End-to-end metric: per-session billed_input_tokens + billed_output_tokens == canonical tokenizer counts for all test sessions (no more than 0.1% drift across 10k sessions)
No duplicate credits or missing credits observed when a stream is paused/resumed by rate limiter or when a model switch occurs mid-stream
All new changes have unit tests, integration tests, and a chaos test with throttling enabled in CI
Rollout plan validated on a canary fleet with traffic shadowing before full release
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run the reproduction harness: scripts/repro/backpressure_harness.py with --clients 200 --mean-chunk-size 64 --backpressure-pattern bursty
2) Configure aggregator to use 10s sliding window and checkpoint compaction enabled
3) Inject artificial rate-limit delay at the serving edge (token-bucket refill rate reduced to 40% for 30s epochs)
4) Force mid-stream model switch on 15% of sessions to trigger fallback and fragment reordering
5) Collect metering audit logs and compare billed token counts against ground-truth tokenizer output
6) Observe sessions with billing discrepancy > 1 token and capture full trace ids
proposed_solution: Threefold approach: 1) Add an idempotent fragment checkpoint identifier emitted by the serving runtime that combines session_id + monotonic_fragment_seq + watermarked_server_timestamp to enable deterministic dedupe in the aggregator. 2) Change aggregator windowing from naive sliding windows to watermark-driven windows that wait for late fragments up to a configurable lateness bound, with explicit out-of-order reconciliation logic. 3) Harden rate-limiter integration so paused/resumed fragments carry a 'pause_boundary' flag and do not reset prefix-credit accounting when resumed; implement a small per-session compaction log to reconcile split prefix contributions.
test_plan: Unit tests for dedupe using fragment checkpoint id permutations
Integration tests: run end-to-end harness in CI with three backpressure profiles (steady, bursty, intermittent)
Chaos test: simulate network reordering and delayed delivery of fragments up to 60s in dedicated stress pipeline
Regression matrix: run previously failing cases from production (capture ids) against the patched aggregator and verify 100% match
Load test: validate no measurable p50/p95 metering latency regressions at 2x baseline traffic
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime-1.20 flag. Deploy aggregator change to canary pool (5%) with shadowed production traffic for 72 hours. Monitor billed token drift, error-rate, and CPU/memory impact. If canary stable, ramp to 25% then 100% over 48-72 hours. Provide rollback knob to disable watermark waiting and revert to current sliding-window logic if regressions observed.
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Patel: Initial triage — found 37 sessions in production with >2 token discrepancy during a 6h incident window. Attached sample traces and initial hypothesis.
2026-03-04 Liam O'Connor: Implemented prototype: serving emits fragment_checkpoint_id and pause_boundary flag. Local unit tests pass dedupe permutations.
2026-03-06 Infra: Verified that canary cluster has capacity for watermark buffering for up to 60s lateness without OOM at projected load; recommended default lateness bound of 30s.
2026-03-08 Design review (Jules Kim): Confirmed UX for accounting breakouts in Console; added requirement to surface dedupe incidents in per-session timeline.
2026-03-10 QA: Integration harness reproduced drift in baseline and shows 0.02% drift after patch in 12k session run. Patching branch ready for PR and canary testing.
notes: Avoid changing token billing semantics during canary; only change dedupe/reconciliation logic so billed units remain stable for customers.
Keep default lateness bound conservative (30s) initially — will tune after canary based on observed late-fragment distribution.
Coordinate with Billing (Sofia Ramos) for final auditing query to validate month-over-month invoice stability after release.
